question:
Before coupling anything: does each half of the co-simulation behave correctly on its own,
and does the particle-to-grid handoff (nearest-node binning, boundary element volumes,
counts to µM) follow vcell-fvsolver's conventions?
hypothesis:
The FV process reproduces continuum diffusion to discretization accuracy. Smoldyn's binned
particle variance grows as 2Dt per axis. Binning conserves molecules exactly. Uniformly
distributed particles give a uniform binned concentration up to and including the
boundary nodes, because boundary elements have 1/2 (edge) or 1/4 (corner) volume as in
VCell's CartesianMesh.
description:
The FV operator is the one in vcell-fvsolver's FV_SOLVER (backward-Euler diffusion,
volume-scaled zero-flux Laplacian); tests/test_grid_and_fv.py checks its discrete
eigenmodes exactly. Here it is compared to the continuum solution. Particle runs use the
full process-bigraph composite (SmoldynHybrid with no fields), so the histogram handoff
is the production path.

variants.name: fv-cosine-mode
variants.diff_from_baseline: FV diffusion of cos(πx/L)cos(πy/L) on 21×21 (L=10 µm, D=1, dt=0.01, t=1 s) vs exp(-2π²Dt/L²).

variants.name: particle-variance
variants.diff_from_baseline: 20,000 particles from the centre cell (D=1, 4 seeds); binned variance − dx²/6 vs 2Dt.

variants.name: boundary-volumes
variants.diff_from_baseline: 100,000 uniform particles after 2 s on 11×11 (4 seeds); per-class counts vs element-volume shares.

simulation_set.name: default
simulation_set.description: Four handoff checks on the shared CartesianGrid; results/metrics.json.

behavior_tests.name: fv-matches-continuum-diffusion
behavior_tests.description: Max relative error of the FV cosine mode vs the analytic decay at t = 1 s.

provenance.note: Second order in space and first order in time; expected error ~1e-3 on this grid.

behavior_tests.name: particle-variance-matches-2Dt
behavior_tests.description: Relative error of the binned per-axis variance (corrected by dx²/6) vs 2Dt at t = 1 s.

provenance.note: Free Brownian motion; 80,000 molecule samples give ~0.5% sampling error on the variance.

behavior_tests.name: histogram-conserves-molecules
behavior_tests.description: Max |histogram total - molecule count| over all records.

provenance.note: Every molecule maps to exactly one node (clamped nearest-node index).

behavior_tests.name: boundary-volumes-give-uniform-concentration
behavior_tests.description: Max |z| over node classes of per-class counts vs element-volume share.

provenance.note: Binomial sampling; |z| < 4 for a correct volume convention (corner 1/4, edge 1/2).

canonical_runs.name: default
canonical_runs.label: FV vs analytic, particle variance vs 2Dt, histogram conservation, boundary volumes

findings.statement: Each half of the co-simulation is correct in isolation: the FV operator reproduces the analytic cosine-mode decay to 6.0e-4 relative error, and Smoldyn's binned per-axis variance (dx²/6-corrected) matches 2Dt to 0.13% relative error at t=1 s.
findings.next_action: None — both solvers verified against their continuum limits.

findings.statement: The particle-to-grid handoff is exact and volume-correct: the histogram total never differs from the molecule count (mismatch = 0 molecules at every record), and uniformly distributed particles bin to a uniform concentration across node classes (max |z| = 0.48; corner and edge concentrations 1.0034× and 1.0019× interior, both within 0.4%), confirming the 1/4-corner and 1/2-edge element-volume convention.
findings.next_action: Proceed to the coupled field-modulated-decay study (pipeline gate satisfied).

regression_compatibility.basis: results/metrics.json is committed and regenerated by sims/run.py; all four primary behavior tests pass against it (FV err 6.0e-4, variance err 0.13%, histogram mismatch 0, boundary max|z| 0.48).

biological_validation.basis: Numerical-convergence study: each half matches its continuum/theoretical limit — FV vs analytic diffusion and binned particle variance vs 2Dt (free Brownian motion).

explanatory_gain.basis: Localizes correctness to the handoff itself: molecule conservation is exact and the boundary element-volume convention (corner 1/4, edge 1/2) yields a uniform binned concentration, so the production composite's particle→grid path is sound.

conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_pass: All four handoff checks pass, so both halves and the particle-to-grid handoff behave as specified: continuum diffusion, 2Dt particle spread, exact molecule conservation, and the VCell element-volume convention at boundaries. The pipeline gate to field-modulated-decay is satisfied — coupling can proceed on a verified foundation.
conclusion_logic.if_primary_tests_fail: An FV error ≥ 1%, a variance error ≥ 3%, any nonzero histogram mismatch, or a boundary max|z| ≥ 4 would mean the FV operator, the particle variance, molecule conservation, or the boundary element-volume convention is wrong — fix the offending half before coupling, since every downstream study inherits this handoff.

rerun.note: Runs the four handoff checks (FV cosine mode, particle variance, histogram conservation, boundary volumes) through the production SmoldynHybrid composite.
